Zero data give the zero weak solution with vanishing compatibility integrals; the zero sheet charge sigma=0 reduces the transmission jump of step 2.2 to [epsilon grad u]=0.

One connected component makes the Neumann compatibility read integral of rho plus boundary g equals zero and the single zero-mean normalisation determine the solution, as recorded in steps 1.2 and 3.1.
Uniform positivity alpha>0, beta<infinity excludes degenerate coefficients, and the Statement and step 3.1 exclude edge, junction, reentrant and coefficient-loss cases from the conclusions.
Boundary values are exact traces supplied by [L1], not endpoint limits, and no condition at infinity occurs because Omega is bounded; the interface conclusions of step 2.2 cover both closed sides.

The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice are those declared by the weak-solvability and regularity suppliers [L1]-[L3] and propagated in the choice accounting of step 3.1; the classical upgrades add no choice.
The forward direction of the Neumann criterion is proved in step 1.2: testing with the constant 1 on a component gives integral rho plus integral g = 0, so the compatibility is necessary.

The reverse direction is the existence clause of [L3] applied in steps 1.2 and 1.3: when the componentwise compatibility (including sheet charges) holds, the weak solution exists, and step 2.1 upgrades it.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used trace and weak Dirichlet-solvability suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k>0$ and $R>0$. Use the sphere-normalised basis $Y^R_{lm}(Rn):=R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ on $S_R$, where $Y_{lm}$ is the complete normalised unit-sphere basis of the spherical-harmonic lemma ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]) and the coefficients $t_l$ are those of the outgoing radial-function lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]). The map

$$T_Rf=\sum_{l,m}t_l\,f_{lm}Y^R_{lm},\qquad f\in H^{1/2}(S_R),$$

is a bounded linear operator $H^{1/2}(S_R)\to H^{-1/2}(S_R)$ with

$$\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle\le0,\qquad\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2>0\quad(f\ne0).$$

It is precisely the outgoing scalar Helmholtz normal derivative at $r=R$: for every $f\in H^{1/2}(S_R)$ the function $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)\,R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ for $r\ge R$ is the unique outgoing finite-local-energy exterior solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$ and normal derivative $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense; it is smooth away from the sphere, and for smooth $f$ it satisfies the ordinary Sommerfeld condition. No uniform pointwise outgoing condition is asserted for arbitrary rough traces; the outgoing condition there is its modal/weak version. Here finite-local-energy means membership in $H^1(\{R<|x|<R_1\})$ for every finite $R_1>R$, with the $H^{1/2}$ trace on $S_R$; no global $H^1$ or global $L^2$ condition at infinity is imposed. The outgoing modal class consists of the displayed outgoing $h_l$ radial factors with no incoming partners; for rough traces this modal class is the definition, rather than a pointwise Sommerfeld assertion. Here the boundary Sobolev spaces are their complex versions (or complexifications of the real trace spaces), $f_{lm}=\int_{S_R}f\overline{Y^R_{lm}}\,d\sigma_R$, and the DtN dual pairing is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second.

Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the modal DtN/trace suppliers, covering the Countable Choice used by the local UCP supplier. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) whose exterior $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ is connected, let $k>0$, and let $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$. Suppose $u$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$, solves $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ on $D$ with the Euclidean Laplacian $\Delta$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), vanishes on $\partial O$, and is outgoing in the class of [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]: its trace $f=u|_{S_R}$ lies in $H^{1/2}(S_R)$ and its normal derivative on $S_R$ is $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense of that lemma. Then $u=0$ on $D$. No decay rate, asymptotic expansion or pointwise Sommerfeld formula beyond the stated outgoing class is assumed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the trace and Sobolev suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^1$ domain, let $\varepsilon$ be a measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic coefficient as in the lift lemma ([[lem-em-lift-specified-dirichlet-existence]]), let $\rho\in L^2(\Omega)$, and prescribe $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)=W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega)$, the fractional Sobolev space of the boundary definition, defined by a finite graph atlas and partition with norm given by the finite sums of localised $L^2$ norms and Gagliardo seminorms ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]], [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]). Then there is exactly one $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $Tu=g$ solving

$$\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=\int_\Omega\rho\,v\qquad\text{for every }v\in H_0^1(\Omega),$$

and the solution depends continuously on $(\rho,g)$: $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|\rho\|_{L^2}+\|g\|_{H^{1/2}})$. The prescribed trace is exact and no classical $C^2$ boundary regularity is inferred.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice inherited from the stated weak-existence, Sobolev extension and trace suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive, and let $\rho$ be smooth on the closure. Prescribe in the prescribed-data lemma either smooth Dirichlet data $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$, or smooth outward flux data $g$ with its compatibility condition as in the weak Neumann lemma. Then the weak solution of $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ in $\Omega$ with those data is $C^\infty$ on the closure $\overline\Omega$. For finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth $\rho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$, the weak solution is smooth on each closed side. Edge and junction points, reentrant corners and coefficient loss of regularity are excluded. The existence claims are those of the two weak solvability lemmas; this lemma proves their classical upgrade on the declared domains.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be nonempty, open and connected, let
$V\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and let
$\psi\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ satisfy $\Delta\psi=V\psi$ in the
distributional sense: $\int_\Omega\psi\,\Delta\varphi\,dx=\int_\Omega V\psi\,\varphi\,dx$
for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, with $\Delta\varphi$ the classical
Laplacian. Here $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ denotes the locally integrable
classes on $\Omega$ whose weak derivatives of every order at most two exist
and are locally square integrable
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]); $V\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$
means that $V$ is measurable and that $\|V\|_\infty<\infty$ on every compact
subset, with the essential supremum of
[[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]] and the space of
[[def-l-infinity-on-a-measure-space]]. If $\psi=0$ on a nonempty open subset
of $\Omega$, then $\psi=0$ on $\Omega$. No smoothness, sign, symmetry or decay
hypothesis on $V$ beyond local essential boundedness is used, and no
analyticity is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open,
$n\ge1$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $L,a$ be as in
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with constants
$\theta,M_a,M_b,M_c$ and with $a^{ij}\in W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)$ satisfying
$\|Da^{ij}\|_\infty\le M_1$, and let $f\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. If
$u\in H^1(\Omega)$ is a local weak solution of $Lu=f$ on $\Omega$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]), then
$u\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and for all open sets
$\Omega'\Subset\Omega''\Subset\Omega$ there is
$C=C(n,\theta,M_a,M_b,M_c,M_1,\Omega',\Omega'')$ with
$$\|u\|_{H^2(\Omega')}\le C\big(\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega'')}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega'')}\big).$$
Consequently the equation $Lu=f$ holds pointwise almost everywhere with
$D_i(a^{ij}D_ju)$ understood through the a.e. defined product
$(D_ia^{ij})D_ju+a^{ij}D_iD_ju$, and the same estimate holds for complex-valued $u$ by taking real parts in the coercive energy bounds; no splitting of complex coefficients into real and imaginary equations is used.
The scaffold wrote $\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ on the
right-hand side, which is ill-posed for a datum known only to lie in
$L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ (for instance $f=1/x$ on $\Omega=(0,1)$ is
locally but not globally square-integrable); the nested formulation above is
the well-posed local statement, and the quantitative content is otherwise
unchanged.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $k\ge0$, and let $L,a$ be as in
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with
$a^{ij}\in W^{k+1,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$,
$b^i,c\in W^{k,\infty}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, all derivatives bounded by
constants $M_\ell$; let $f\in H^k_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ and let
$u\in H^1(\Omega)$ be a local weak solution of $Lu=f$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]). Then
$u\in H^{k+2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and for all open sets
$\Omega'\Subset\Omega''\Subset\Omega$ there is
$C=C(n,\theta,k,M_0,\dots,M_{k+1},\Omega',\Omega'')$ with
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}(\Omega')}\le C\big(\|f\|_{H^k(\Omega'')}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega'')}\big).$$
The gain is exactly two derivatives; the coefficient regularity required is
one order above the data order. For $k=0$ the theorem reduces to
[[thm-interior-h-two-regularity-for-divergence-form-equations]]. The
scaffold wrote $\|f\|_{H^k(\Omega)}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ on the right-hand
side, which is ill-posed for locally Sobolev data on an unbounded $\Omega$;
the nested formulation is the well-posed local statement.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and let $f$ be a bounded linear functional on $H$ ([[def-dual-space-of-a-normed-space]]). Then there is a unique $y\in H$ with

$$f(x)=\langle x,y\rangle\qquad\text{for every }x\in H,$$

and $\|f\|=\|y\|$, where $\|f\|$ is the dual norm ([[def-operator-norm]]). Under the first-variable-linear convention the representing vector depends conjugate-linearly and isometrically on $f$: if $f_i$ is represented by $y_i$ and $a,b$ are scalars, then $af_1+bf_2$ is represented by $\overline a\,y_1+\overline b\,y_2$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a Banach space
over a fixed field $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $K:X\to X$ be a compact operator
([[def-compact-linear-operator]]) and put $A:=I-K$. Then:

1. $A$ is injective if and only if it is surjective, and in that case $A$ is
   boundedly invertible;
2. for every $y\in X$ the equation $Ax=y$ has a solution if and only if
   $\varphi(y)=0$ for every $\varphi\in\ker A^*$, the transpose
   $A^*=I-K^*$ acting on $X^*$
   ([[def-transpose-of-a-bounded-operator]]);
3. $\ker A$ and the cokernel $X/\operatorname{ran}A$
   ([[def-quotient-vector-space-coset-notation]]) are finite dimensional with
   equal dimensions over $F$ ([[def-dimension]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain in the graph sense of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], let $\partial\Omega$ carry the
chart-independent surface measure of
[[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] and
[[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]], let
$1\le p<\infty$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then there is a
unique bounded linear operator
$$T:W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow L^p(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$$
with $Tu=u|_{\partial\Omega}$ for every
$u\in C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and it satisfies
$\|Tu\|_{L^p(\partial\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$. On each
boundary chart the operator is the flat half-space trace of
[[thm-trace-estimate-on-the-half-space]] transported by the flattening
diffeomorphism, and the chartwise definitions agree on overlaps; uniqueness
holds because two bounded operators agreeing on the dense subspace
$C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ are equal.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $p'=p/(p-1)$,
$u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, $v\in W^{1,p'}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let
$T$ be the trace of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] with
$\nu$ the outward normal of
[[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. Then for
every $i=1,\dots,n$,
$$\int_\Omega u\,\partial_iv\,dx=-\int_\Omega(\partial_iu)v\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega}(Tu)(Tv)\,\nu_i\,dS,$$
and all three integrals are finite. If $u,v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, the
boundary term is the classical $\int_{\partial\Omega}uv\,\nu_i\,dS$ of the
divergence theorem
[[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]] applied to the
field $uv\,e_i$; if in addition $Tu=\partial_\nu w$ on $\partial\Omega$ for a specified $w\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, the boundary term is $\int_{\partial\Omega}(\partial_\nu w)(Tv)\nu_i\,dS$. The normal derivative of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]] is defined on the boundary, and this extra identity is an assumption, not an interior substitution.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge2$, $d=n-1$, $1\le p<\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$H=\{x=(x',x_n)\in\mathbb R^n:x_n>0\}$ with
$\partial H=\mathbb R^d\times\{0\}$. Write $\partial_n$ for the last
coordinate derivative.

(i) For every $u\in C(\overline H)\cap W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)$ with compact
support, the classical boundary function $g=u(\cdot,0)$ satisfies
$$|g(x')|^p\le p\int_0^\infty|u(x',t)|^{p-1}\,|\partial_nu(x',t)|\,dt$$
for a.e. $x'\in\mathbb R^d$, hence
$\|g\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}^p\le p\,\|u\|_{L^p(H)}^{p-1}\|\partial_nu\|_{L^p(H)}\le p\,\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}^p$.
For every $h>0$ the strip form
$$h\,|g(x')|^p\le C_p\Bigl(\int_0^h|u(x',t)|^pdt+h^p\int_0^h|\partial_nu(x',t)|^pdt\Bigr)$$
holds for a.e. $x'$, with $C_p=2^{p-1}$ for $1<p<\infty$ and $C_1=1$.

(ii) There is a unique bounded linear operator
$T_+:W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)\to L^p(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb K)$ with
$T_+u=u(\cdot,0)$ for every compactly supported
$u\in C(\overline H)\cap W^{1,p}(H)$, and
$\|T_+u\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}\le C(n,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}$; it is the unique
bounded extension of classical restriction, and $T_+u$ depends only on the
a.e. class of $u$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k\ge1$, $1\le p\le\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a
bounded $C^k$ domain in the graph sense of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. Then for every open set
$V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\overline\Omega\subseteq V$ there is a bounded
linear extension operator
$$E:W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K),\qquad (Eu)|_\Omega=u\ \text{a.e. on }\Omega,$$
such that $\operatorname{supp}(Eu)$ is a compact subset of $V$ for every
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. In particular each bounded $C^k$ domain is a
$W^{k,p}$-extension domain, with an operator whose output is supported in any
prescribed neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$. For $k=0$, extension by zero
is an isometric $L^p$ extension on any open $\Omega$; its output is supported
in the compact set $\overline\Omega\subseteq V$ when $\Omega$ is bounded.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a
bounded extension domain, let $1\le p<n$, $p^{*}=\frac{np}{n-p}$, and let
$(u_j)$ be bounded in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ with $u_j\rightharpoonup u$ weakly in
$W^{1,p}(\Omega)$. Then $u_j\to u$ in $L^q(\Omega)$ for every $1\le q<p^{*}$;
the convergence is of the whole sequence, not merely of a subsequence.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same field
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, read in the real case from
[[def-norm-and-normed-space]] and in the complex case from
[[rem-real-and-complex-normed-space-convention]], and suppose $X\subseteq Y$
with **continuous inclusion** $J:X\to Y$: there is a real $C\ge0$ with
$\|x\|_Y\le C\|x\|_X$ for every $x\in X$.

One says that $X$ is **compactly embedded** in $Y$, written $X\Subset Y$, when
the inclusion operator $J$ is a compact operator in the sense of
[[def-compact-linear-operator]]: the image under $J$ of every bounded
subset of $X$ ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]) has compact closure in $Y$
([[def-metric-compactness]]).

**The sequential form.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]) and the Axiom of Dependent Choice
([[def-dependent-choice]]). Then $X\Subset Y$ if and only if every bounded
sequence $(x_j)$ in $X$ has a subsequence $(x_{j_k})$ converging in $Y$:
Indeed, compact closure gives the sequence conclusion by
[[thm-metric-compactness-equivalences]]. Conversely, fix bounded $B\subseteq X$
and let $K=\overline{J(B)}$. For any sequence $(y_j)$ in $K$, Countable
Choice selects $b_j\in B$ with $\|y_j-b_j\|_Y<1/j$ (start at $j=1$);
a convergent subsequence of $(b_j)$ gives one of $(y_j)$ with the same limit,
which belongs to the closed set $K$. Thus $K$ is sequentially compact and
[[thm-metric-compactness-equivalences]] makes it compact. The empty case is
immediate. Both readings
of $X\Subset Y$ are used on this page; the second is the form in which the
compactness theorems below are stated.

Continuity of the inclusion is a separate hypothesis and is never inferred
from compactness: a compact operator is bounded by
[[def-compact-linear-operator]] and [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], but the
definition above fixes the continuity of $J$ in advance. On this page the
continuity of every Sobolev inclusion is verified separately, through the
corresponding Sobolev embedding theorem.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $1\le p\le\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R)$ with
$M_\eta:=\|D\eta\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)}$ and compact support; the case
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ is read by extending $\eta$ by zero.
Then for every $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ and every $h\ne0$, on the shrunken set
$\Omega_{i,h}=\{x\in\Omega:x+he_i\in\Omega\}$ of
[[def-first-difference-quotient]] one has the exact identity
$$\delta_h^i(\eta u)-\eta\,\delta_h^iu=(\delta_h^i\eta)\,(\tau_{-he_i}u)\qquad\text{a.e. on }\Omega_{i,h},$$
where $\tau$ is the published translation $\tau_hu(x)=u(x-h)$ of
[[def-translation-of-a-function-on-rn]], so that
$(\tau_{-he_i}u)(x)=u(x+he_i)$. Consequently
$$\|\delta_h^i(\eta u)-\eta\,\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(\Omega_{i,h})}\le M_\eta\,\|\tau_{-he_i}u\|_{L^p(\Omega_{i,h})}\le M_\eta\,\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)},$$
and more generally, on the domain where both sides are defined,
$$\delta_h^i\big(\eta^2\delta_h^iu\big)=\eta^2\delta_h^i\delta_h^iu+(\delta_h^i\eta^2)\,(\tau_{-he_i}\delta_h^iu).$$
The statement is quantitative in $\|D\eta\|_{L^\infty}$ and does not assume
any regularity of $u$ beyond $W^{1,p}$.

**Sobolev multiplier and support facts used below.** For every integer
$m\ge0$, $q\in W^{m,\infty}(U)$ and $z\in H^m(U)$ on an open set $U$,
$qz\in H^m(U)$ and
$$D^\alpha(qz)=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha}{\alpha\choose\beta}(D^\beta q)D^{\alpha-\beta}z,\qquad |\alpha|\le m,$$
with $\|qz\|_{H^m(U)}\le C(n,m)\|q\|_{W^{m,\infty}(U)}\|z\|_{H^m(U)}$.
Also, every compactly supported $z\in H^m(U)$ lies in $H^m_0(U)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Then:

1. if $kp<n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every $q$ with $\frac1q\ge\frac1p-\frac kn$ (equivalently $1\le q\le\frac{np}{n-kp}$);
2. if $kp=n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(q)\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every finite $q$;
3. if $kp>n$, then for every integer $m\ge0$ and every $0<\alpha<1$ with $m+\alpha<k-\frac np$ there is a representative in $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$; when $k-\frac np\notin\mathbb Z$ one may take $m=\lfloor k-\frac np\rfloor$ and $\alpha=k-\frac np-m$.

Here $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uses the continuous derivatives of the constructed representative on an ambient neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$, with norm
$$\|g\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\beta|\le m}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta g|+\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|D^\beta g(x)-D^\beta g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For $\Omega=\varnothing$ set these norm values to $0$. The proof supplies such an ambient representative, so no boundary differentiability or regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is assumed.

If $f,g\in\mathcal L^2(\mu)$, then

$$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_2\|g\|_2.$$

Equality holds if and only if at least one of $f,g$ is zero almost everywhere,
or there is a constant $c>0$ with

$$|f|^2=c\,|g|^2\qquad\mu\text{-almost everywhere}.$$
If $f$ is $C^2$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$, then $\partial_i\partial_j f=\partial_j\partial_i f$ for every pair of coordinate indices.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$ and $\theta=1-1/p$, with
$W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$ as in
[[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]. Then the trace
operator $T$ of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] satisfies
$$\|Tu\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)} \qquad(u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)),$$
and it is onto: $T(W^{1,p}(\Omega))=W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$. For $p>1$
the range is a strict subset of $L^p(\partial\Omega)$, and the trace is not a
compact operator into $W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, used to invoke the published real and complex
$L^p$ completeness results through their Countable-Choice interface. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$1\le p\le\infty$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, equipped with the displayed norm of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], is a complete normed space over
$\mathbb K$.

Both endpoints $p=1$ and $p=\infty$ are included, as is $k=0$, where the
assertion reduces to the completeness of $L^p$. If $\Omega=\varnothing$, then
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is the zero space and the assertion is trivial.
The Axiom of Choice is used only to derive Countable Choice for the two
published completeness interfaces; no other selection is made. Representative
selection inside the finitely many coordinate classes is finite and
choice-free.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a **bounded smooth graph domain**: a nonempty bounded open set such that for every $x\in\partial\Omega$ there are an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ of $x$, a rigid motion $R(p)=Qp+b$, an open ball $B\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ and a function $h\in C^\infty(B;\mathbb R)$ such that, after shrinking $W$ so that $R(W)\subseteq B\times\mathbb R$,

$$R(\Omega\cap W)=R(W)\cap\{(y,s)\in B\times\mathbb R:s<h(y)\},$$

which is the $C^\infty$ case of the bounded $C^k$ graph domain of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. Let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open set with $\overline\Omega\subseteq V$. Then there exists a real-linear operator $E_\Omega$, determined only by $\Omega$, a finite smooth atlas and fixed cutoffs, such that for every open interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) and every function $u:\Omega\times J\to\mathbb R$ that is of class $C^\infty$ on the open set $\Omega\times J$ and whose every mixed derivative $D^\alpha\partial_\tau^j u:\Omega\times J\to\mathbb R$ has a continuous extension to $\overline\Omega\times J$ ([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), the function $E_\Omega u$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times J$, satisfies $E_\Omega u(x,\tau)=u(x,\tau)$ for all $(x,\tau)\in\overline\Omega\times J$ and

$$D^\alpha\partial_\tau^j(E_\Omega u)\big|_{\overline\Omega\times J}=\text{the continuous extension of }D^\alpha\partial_\tau^j u$$

for all multi-indices $\alpha$ and all $j\ge0$, and is spatially supported in one fixed compact subset of $V$, in the sense that there is a compact $K_\Omega\subseteq V$ with $E_\Omega u(x,\tau)=0$ for all $x\notin K_\Omega$, $\tau\in J$. For every compact $K\subseteq J$, every integer $m\ge0$ and every $j\ge0$,

$$\sup_{\tau\in K}\|\partial_\tau^j E_\Omega u(\cdot,\tau)\|_{C^m(\mathbb R^3)}\le C_m\sup_{\tau\in K}\|\partial_\tau^j u(\cdot,\tau)\|_{C^m(\overline\Omega)},$$

where $\|w\|_{C^m(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\alpha|\le m}\sup_{x\in\overline\Omega}|D^\alpha w(x)|$ and $\|W\|_{C^m(\mathbb R^3)}:=\sum_{|\alpha|\le m}\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^3}|D^\alpha W(x)|$, and the constant $C_m$ depends only on $m$, $\Omega$, the atlas and cutoffs. The extension commutes with every time derivative: $\partial_\tau^j(E_\Omega u)=E_\Omega(\partial_\tau^j u)$ for all $j\ge0$. No bound uniform over an unbounded $J$ is asserted. Vector-valued inputs of finite dimension are extended componentwise. The construction adds no choice principle: the finite atlas is selected from the cover of all admissible smooth chart patches, finite cutoffs come from the published choice-free compact cutoff lemma, and the infinite coefficient sequence is defined by the explicit formula below. The consuming elliptic or Sobolev argument retains whatever choice principles its own suppliers declare.

derivations.claim:
**Collar trace inequality on the inner boundary.** For every $\delta>0$ there is $C_\delta$ such that every $u\in H^1(A;\mathbb C^3)$ satisfies $\|u\|_{L^2(\partial O)}^2\le\delta\|
abla u\|_{L^2(A)}^2+C_\delta\|u\|_{L^2(A)}^2$. Indeed, cover $\partial O$ by finitely many flattening charts of the smooth boundary ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) and let $\chi$ be a smooth cutoff, equal to $1$ near $\partial O$ and supported in the resulting collar. On the collar, in normal coordinates $x=\Phi(y,t)$ with $t$ proportional to the distance to $\partial O$, the strip estimate [L12] with $p=2$, divided by $h$ and integrated over $y$ with the bounded chart Jacobians, gives $\|u\chi\|_{L^2(\partial O)}^2\le C(h^{-1}\|u\chi\|_{L^2(A)}^2+h\|
abla(u\chi)\|_{L^2(A)}^2)$ for every smooth $u$; choosing $h$ so small that $2Ch\le\delta$, expanding $
abla(u\chi)=\chi
abla u+u
abla\chi$ and absorbing the cutoff terms into $C_\delta\|u\|_{L^2(A)}^2$ yields the claim for smooth $u$, and both sides are continuous in the $H^1(A)$ norm (boundary term by [L10]), while products of global $C_c^\infty$ approximations with a fixed cutoff are dense in the $H^1$ classes supported in the collar by [[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]] and [L13]; the inequality therefore extends to all $u\in H^1(A;\mathbb C^3)$.

**Smooth componentwise lift of the tangential datum.** For $j=1,2,3$ let $(e_T)_j\in C^\infty(\partial O)$ be the Cartesian components of $e_T$ and extend them by zero to $\partial A=\partial O\cup S_R$, obtaining smooth functions $g_j\in C^\infty(\partial A)$. By [L3] with $\varepsilon=I$, $\rho=0$, applied separately to the real and imaginary parts, there is a unique $G_j\in H^1(A)$ with trace $g_j$ and $\int_A\nabla\overline v\cdot\nabla G_j=0$ for all $v\in H_0^1(A)$; by [L4] with $\rho=0$ and the smooth Dirichlet data $g_j$, each $G_j$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline A$, is harmonic on $A$, and $G_j|_{\partial A}=g_j$. Hence $G:=(G_1,G_2,G_3)$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline A$, satisfies $\Delta G=0$ componentwise, $G|_{\partial O}=e_T$ and $G|_{S_R}=0$, and is tangential on $\partial O$.

**Coercivity of the shifted form.** With $\lambda:=\|\kappa\|_\infty(1+C_1)+k^2+1$, where $C_1$ is the constant of step 1.2 for $\delta:=\tfrac12(\|\kappa\|_\infty+1)^{-1}$, one has $\operatorname{Re}(a(E,E)+\lambda\|E\|_{L^2(A)}^2)\ge c\|E\|_{H^1(A)}^2$ for every $E\in X$, with $c=\tfrac12$. Indeed $\operatorname{Re}a(E,E)=\|\nabla E\|_2^2-k^2\|E\|_2^2+\int_{\partial O}\kappa|E_n|^2-\operatorname{Re}\langle T_RE,E\rangle$; the last term is nonnegative by $\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle\le0$ of [L1] applied componentwise to $f=E|_{S_R}$; and the boundary term obeys $|\int_{\partial O}\kappa|E_n|^2|\le\|\kappa\|_\infty\|E\|_{L^2(\partial O)}^2\le\tfrac12\|\nabla E\|_2^2+\|\kappa\|_\infty C_1\|E\|_2^2$ by step 1.2 and [L19].

**The shifted form is boundedly invertible.** By the Riesz representation theorem [L8], applied to the bounded conjugate-linear functional $v\mapsto a(E,v)+\lambda(E,v)_{L^2}$ on the complete space $X$, the shifted form is represented by a bounded linear operator $S:X\to X$ with $\operatorname{Re}\langle Sx,x\rangle\ge c\|x\|^2$ and $\|S\|\le M$ for constants $c,M>0$ (step 2.1 and step 1.1). Choose $0<t<2c/M^2$ and put $q:=\sqrt{1-2tc+t^2M^2}<1$. For $x,y\in X$, $\|(I-tS)(x-y)\|^2\le q^2\|x-y\|^2$ by expanding the square and using [L19]; hence for every $f\in X$ the iteration $x_{n+1}:=(I-tS)x_n+tf$ is a strict contraction of the complete space $X$, so $\|x_{n+1}-x_n\|\le q^n\|x_1-x_0\|$. The geometric tail estimate makes $(x_n)$ Cauchy; completeness supplies its limit $x$, continuity gives $x=(I-tS)x+tf$ and $Sx=f$, and the same contraction inequality makes the fixed point unique. If $Sx=0$ then $c\|x\|^2\le\operatorname{Re}\langle Sx,x\rangle=0$, so $x=0$; thus $S$ is boundedly invertible with $\|S^{-1}\|\le c^{-1}$.

**Compactness of the $L^2$ pairing and the Fredholm reduction.** Use the Riesz identification fixed in step 3.1 and let $J:X\to X$ be the represented $L^2$ pairing, $\langle Jx,v\rangle_X=(x,v)_{L^2(A)}$. A conjugate-linear functional in $v$ is represented here by applying [L8] to its complex conjugate and then conjugating the pairing, so this identification is linear in $x$. The inclusion $X\hookrightarrow H^1(A;\mathbb C^3)$ is continuous and $A$ is a bounded $W^{1,2}$-extension domain [L13], so by [L14] with $p=2<n=3$ every bounded sequence in $H^1(A)$ has an $L^2$-convergent subsequence; by [L16] the Countable and Dependent Choice assumptions of the sequential criterion [L15] are available, so the inclusion $H^1(A)\hookrightarrow L^2(A)$ is compact, and so is its restriction $X\hookrightarrow L^2(A)$, hence also the composition $J$ of that restriction with the bounded represented pairing $L^2(A)\to X$. Therefore $K:=S^{-1}J:X\to X$ is compact, and the operator $A_{\mathrm{op}}:=S-\lambda J$ represented by $a$ satisfies $S^{-1}A_{\mathrm{op}}=I-\lambda K$; by the Fredholm alternative [L9] the operator $S^{-1}A_{\mathrm{op}}$ is boundedly invertible as soon as its kernel is trivial, and its kernel consists exactly of the $E\in X$ with $a(E,v)=0$ for all $v\in X$.

**Bounded invertibility of $a$.** By step 3.2 the kernel of $S^{-1}A_{\mathrm{op}}=I-\lambda K$ is trivial, so the Fredholm alternative [L9] makes it boundedly invertible; hence $A_{\mathrm{op}}=S(I-\lambda K)$ and the form $a$ are boundedly invertible: for every bounded conjugate-linear functional $F$ on $X$ there is exactly one $E\in X$ with $a(E,v)=F(v)$ for all $v\in X$, and $\|E\|_{H^1(A)}\le C\|F\|_{X^*}$.

**The weak solution with prescribed tangential trace.** Define on $X$ the functional $F(v):=-a(G,v)-\int_{\partial O}(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T)\overline{v_n}\,dS$. Both summands are bounded in $v$: the first by step 1.1, the second because $\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T\in C^\infty(\partial O)$ and $v\mapsto v_n|_{\partial O}$ is trace-continuous into $L^2(\partial O)$ by [L10], applied in the boundary charts. By step 5.1 there is exactly one $u\in X$ with $a(u,v)=F(v)$ for all $v\in X$; set $E:=G+u\in H^1(A;\mathbb C^3)$. Then $E_{\text{tangential}}=e_T$ on $\partial O$ because $u\in X$ and $G$ is tangential there, and testing the defining identity with $v$ compactly supported in the interior of $A$ gives $-\Delta E=k^2E$ weakly on $A$. Moreover, for every $v\in X$ supported away from $\partial O$ one has $a(E,v)=a(G,v)+a(u,v)=-\int_{\partial O}(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T)\overline{v_n}\,dS=0$, so the same integration-by-parts computation as in step 3.2 shows that the normal trace of $E$ on $S_R$ equals $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense, where $f=E|_{S_R}=u|_{S_R}\in H^{1/2}(S_R;\mathbb C^3)$.

**Gluing across the artificial sphere and smoothness on the open set $D$.** Let $E_{\mathrm{out}}$ be the outgoing series of [L1] built from the trace $f=E|_{S_R}$, defined on $\{|x|>R\}$; by [L1] it is a finite-local-energy solution there with normal derivative $T_Rf$, and it is smooth away from the sphere. Define $\widetilde E:=E$ on $A$ and $\widetilde E:=E_{\mathrm{out}}$ on $\{|x|>R\}$. The two pieces have the same trace $f$ on $S_R$; applying the Sobolev-Gauss-Green formula [L11] on $A$ and on the exterior annulus $B_M\setminus\overline B_R$ (with the outward normals $+n$ and $-n$ on $S_R$) and adding, the two interface pairings cancel, so $\widetilde E\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$ with weak gradient the two-sided gradient. For every test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(D)$ the weak equations on both sides then give $\int_D\nabla\widetilde E:\overline{\nabla\varphi}=k^2\int_D\widetilde E\cdot\overline\varphi$: on $A$ this is the weak identity of step 6.1, on the exterior it is the weak Helmholtz equation satisfied by the outgoing series, and the interface terms have cancelled. Since $k^2\widetilde E\in H^k_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$ for every $k$ as soon as $\widetilde E\in H^k_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$, repeated application of the interior gain-two estimate [L7] starting from $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ gives $\widetilde E\in H^m_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$ for every $m$, hence a $C^\infty(D)$ representative satisfying the classical Helmholtz equation on $D$.

**Homogeneous tangential traces before boundary localization.** Put $u:=E-G$, with the smooth harmonic lift $G$ of step 1.3; by step 6.1, $u\in X$, so its tangential trace on $\partial O$ is zero. Fix a smooth normal collar chart with coordinates $(y,s)$, $s<0$ in $A$, and a smooth orthonormal frame $Q=(\tau_1,\tau_2,n)$ extended constantly along its normal lines. Write $u=QU$; thus $U_1=U_2=0$ on the flat boundary. The weak identity for $u$ is $a(u,v)=-a(G,v)-\int_{\partial O}(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T)\overline{v_n}$. Since $\Delta G=0$, integrating the smooth lift term by parts in a chart away from $S_R$ gives the smooth volume datum $k^2G$ and normal boundary datum $-\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T-\partial_nG_n$ (the trace $G_n$ is zero and $\partial_n n=0$). Transporting and localizing this identity by a cutoff $\eta$ gives, for every compactly localized $H^1$ test $V$ with $V_1=V_2=0$ on the flat boundary, $$\sum_m\int a^{ij}\partial_jU_m\overline{\partial_iV_m}+\int_B\beta U_3\overline{V_3}=\int f\cdot\overline V+\sum_i\int G_i\cdot\overline{\partial_iV}+\int_Bh\overline{V_3}.$$ The principal matrix $a^{ij}$ is smooth, uniformly positive and scalar in $m$, since $Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I$; $\beta=\kappa J_B$ is smooth and possibly signed; $f=k^2J(U+Q^{\mathsf T}G)+(\text{smooth})U+(\text{smooth})\partial U\in L^2$; $G_i=(\text{smooth})U$ plus smooth lift/cutoff terms belongs to $H^1$; and $h=-(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T+\partial_nG_n)\circ\psi\,J_B$ times the localized cutoff is smooth. Tests are admissible: their first two components have zero trace, so odd reflection of those components and even reflection of the third, followed by parity-preserving mollification and cutoff, approximate them in $H^1$; pulling back the smooth frame and chart and extending by zero produces fields in $X$. The difference-quotient tests below therefore act on $U$, whose first two traces actually vanish, rather than on $Q^{\mathsf T}E$ with its prescribed nonzero traces.

**Tangential second derivatives and recovery of the normal derivatives.** Let $k\in\{1,2\}$ be a tangential direction, put $W:=\delta_h^kU=(U(y+he_k,s)-U(y,s))/h$ and test the system of step 7.2 with $V:=-\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2W)$ on a nested pair of half-boxes; this test has $V_1=V_2=0$ on $B$ and compact support, so it is admissible. The discrete integration by parts of [L17] and the shifted product rule give a principal term bounded below by $\alpha\|\eta
abla W\|_{L^2}^2$ with $\alpha>0$ the ellipticity constant of $a^{ij}$, while all remaining terms involve $\delta_h a$, $
abla\eta$, $W$, $
abla U$, $f$ or the transferred quotients of $G$, and are bounded by $\epsilon\|\eta
abla W\|_2^2+C_\epsilon(\|U\|_{H^1}^2+\|f\|_{L^2}^2+\|G\|_{H^1}^2)$ using [L17], the increment estimate $\|\delta_h^kU\|_{L^2}\le\|\partial_kU\|_{L^2}$, and [L19]. On $B$ the Robin term gives $\int_B eta(y+he_k)\eta^2|W_3|^2+\int_B(\delta_h^k eta)U_3\eta^2\overline{W_3}$; the trace estimate $\|Tz\|_{L^2(B)}^2\le\epsilon\|
abla z\|_{L^2}^2+C_\epsilon\|z\|_{L^2}^2$ of step 1.2 (with $B$ the flattened $\partial O$) absorbs the first term for either sign of $ eta$, and bounded $\delta_h eta$, the trace bound for $U_3$ and [L19] bound the second; the smooth datum $h$ contributes $\int_B(\delta_h^kh)\overline{W_3}$, bounded by $\|h\|_{H^1(B)}\|T(\eta^2W_3)\|_{L^2(B)}$ and absorbed in the same way. Choosing the finitely many $\epsilon$ small gives $\|\eta
abla\delta_h^kU\|_{L^2}\le C(\|U\|_{H^1}+\|f\|_{L^2}+\|G\|_{H^1}+\|h\|_{H^1(B)})$ uniformly in $h$, hence every tangential second derivative of $U$ lies in $L^2$ after the limit argument in which the bounded functional $\psi\mapsto\lim_h\int(\partial_iU_m)\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2\psi)$ is represented in $L^2$ by [L8]. From the interior equation $-\partial_i(a^{ij}\partial_jU_m)=f_m-\partial_iG_{i,m}$ one then recovers $a^{33}\partial_{ss}U_m=\partial_iG_{i,m}-f_m-\sum_{(i,j)
e(3,3)}a^{ij}\partial_{ij}U_m-\sum_{i,j}(\partial_ia^{ij})\partial_jU_m$, whose right side is now $L^2$ and whose coefficient satisfies $a^{33}\ge\alpha>0$; so all second derivatives of $U$ lie in $L^2$ on the smaller half-box, and a finite cover of the compact boundary gives $u\in H^2$ up to $\partial O$ and hence $E=u+G\in H^2$, since $G$ is smooth.

**Higher-order bootstrap and the classical boundary conclusion.** Suppose $U\in H^{r+1}$ on the larger half-box for some $r\ge1$; the data of the local system then satisfy $f\in H^r$, each divergence datum $G_i\in H^{r+1}$ and the lift-adjusted boundary datum $h$ is smooth because all coefficients are smooth. For a tangential multi-index $\alpha$ of order $r$ put $Z:=D_y^\alpha U$; differentiating the system of step 7.2 by $D_y^\alpha$ keeps the principal matrix $a^{ij}$ and the Robin coefficient $\beta$, and replaces the data by $f_\alpha\in L^2$, $G_\alpha\in H^1$ and $h_\alpha\in H^1(B)$ built from $D_y^\alpha f$, $D_y^\alpha G$ and the finitely many commutator terms $D_y^\gamma(\text{coefficient})\,D_y^{\alpha-\gamma}U$ with $0<\gamma\le\alpha$, all known by the induction hypothesis; the tangential traces of $Z$ are again zero in the first two components and free in the third, and localized tests for $Z$ are admissible by the test approximation of step 7.2; the differentiated Robin commutators contain traces of tangential derivatives of $U$ of order at most $r-1$, their tangential derivatives of one further order have $L^2$ traces because the corresponding interior derivatives of order at most $r$ belong to $H^1$; trace continuity and smooth approximation therefore place those commutators in $H^1(B)$ by [L10]. Applying step 8.1 to $Z$ gains two further tangential or mixed derivatives, and differentiating the normal-recovery equation of step 8.1 and inducting on the number of normal derivatives recovers the remaining ones; nested half-boxes and a finite boundary cover give $U\in H^m$ on each smaller patch for every $m$, with constants depending on the data, $\kappa$, the chart and the fixed nested covers. By the Sobolev embedding [L18] on a rounded bounded smooth subdomain of the chart that agrees with $s=0$ near the smaller patch and lies inside the larger half-box (hence an extension domain by [L13]) each $H^m$ class with $m>j+\tfrac32$ has a $C^j$ representative on the closed patch, compatible for different $j$; hence $u$, and therefore $E=u+G$, has all derivatives continuous up to $\partial O$; combining with the smooth gluing at $S_R$, [L22] on the bounded annulus $A$ supplies one smooth ambient representative near its closure, and the classical integration by parts in the local frame (equivalently [L11] with classical traces) turns $a(E,v)=-\int_{\partial O}(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T)\overline{v_n}$ for admissible inner-collar tests into the boundary identities $\partial_nE_n+\kappa E_n=-\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T$ and $E_{\text{tangential}}=e_T$ on $\partial O$.

**The divergence constraint.** Let $q:=\operatorname{div}E$ on $D$. By step 9.1 and step 7.1, $E\in C^\infty(\overline D;\mathbb C^3)$ once the two-sided solution is matched at $S_R$; the mixed partials commute [L20], so $\Delta q=\operatorname{div}\Delta E=-k^2\operatorname{div}E=-k^2q$ on $D$. On $\partial O$ the exact boundary identity $\operatorname{div}E=\partial_nE_n+(\operatorname{div}n)E_n+\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}E_{\text{tangential}}$ holds in the classical sense with the chosen normal extension, and its first two terms sum to $-\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T$ by step 9.1 while the third equals $\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T$; hence $q=0$ on $\partial O$. Finally $q$ is outgoing in the class of [L1]: on $\{|x|>R\}$ the field $E$ equals the outgoing series of [L1] by the uniqueness clause of that lemma, and differentiating the series componentwise in the spherical-harmonic expansion and using the spherical-Bessel recurrences $h_l'=h_{l-1}-(l+1)h_l/z$ and $h_l/z=(h_{l-1}+h_{l+1})/(2l+1)$ (which follow from the finite polynomial expression for $h_l$) expresses every radial factor of $q$ as a finite combination of outgoing factors $h_{l'}(kr)$, $l'\in\{l-1,l,l+1\}$; so $q$ has no incoming modal component and satisfies $\partial_rq=T_R(q|_{S_R})$ on $S_R$ in the class of [L1]. The exterior scalar uniqueness lemma [L2] applies to $q$ on the connected $D$ and gives $q=0$ on $D$, that is, the divergence constraint.

**Uniqueness of the classical problem.** Let $E_1,E_2\in C^\infty(\overline D;\mathbb C^3)$ both satisfy the conditions of the Statement. Their difference $W:=E_1-E_2$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$, solves $(\Delta+k^2)W=0$ componentwise on $D$, has $\operatorname{div}W=0$ and $W_{\text{tangential}}=0$ on $\partial O$, and is outgoing on $S_R$. Then $W\in X$ with $W|_{S_R}\in H^{1/2}$, and the integration by parts of step 3.2 and step 6.1 shows that $a(W,v)=0$ for every $v\in X$: the volume terms reproduce the Helmholtz equation, the inner boundary term cancels against $\operatorname{div}W=0$ on $\partial O$ through the exact identity of step 10.1, and the outer term cancels because $\partial_rW=T_R(W|_{S_R})$ by outgoingness. By step 3.2, $W=0$ on $D$.

**Assembly and choice accounting.** Existence is step 6.1 together with the regularity and gluing of steps 7.1, 8.1 and 9.1: the constructed $E=G+u$ has the prescribed tangential trace, satisfies $(\Delta+k^2)E=0$ on $D$, is $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$ and outgoing on $S_R$ in the stated weak trace sense, and satisfies the closure relation of step 9.1; its divergence vanishes by step 10.1. Uniqueness is step 11.1. The only choice principle used is the Axiom of Choice assumed in the Statement: it supplies the Fredholm alternative, and through [L16] the Countable and Dependent Choice invoked by the compactness, trace and difference-quotient interfaces [L15], [L10], [L12], [L17]; the lift, the coercive inversion and the boundary bootstrap make only finitely many explicit selections. This proves all assertions.

boundaries.evidence: The empty tangential datum case is the homogeneous problem: e_T=0 makes the lift G of step 1.3 zero, and the kernel analysis of steps 3.2 and 5.1 gives the identically zero solution, consistent with the existence and uniqueness claims.
The zero datum returns u=0 through steps 1.3, 5.1 and 6.1; uniqueness in step 11.1 then forces every solution with zero tangential trace and the closure relation to be zero.

A single nonzero tangential mode cannot survive the homogeneous kernel: the imaginary part of the form in step 3.2 forces the full trace f=0 on S_R, and the extension argument of that step then gives the zero solution.

Degeneracies are excluded and used exactly where needed: the C-infinity boundary makes the flattening charts of step 7.2 available, kappa=div n is smooth and bounded in steps 2.1 and 1.2, and connectedness of D is consumed only in step 3.2.

The artificial sphere S_R is an interior interface: step 7.1 glues the two pieces by matching traces and normal derivatives, and no endpoint at infinity, decay rate or pointwise Sommerfeld formula beyond the modal class is charged.

The Axiom of Choice is assumed in the statement; it is consumed through the Fredholm alternative [L9] at steps 4.1 and 5.1 and, via [L16], supplies the Countable and Dependent Choice used by [L15], [L10], [L12] and [L17].

boundaries.reason: The lemma is an existence-and-uniqueness assertion with a closure relation, not a biconditional; there is no forward direction of an equivalence to discharge.
No converse criterion is asserted: the lemma does not claim that arbitrary boundary data or arbitrary normal traces arise from some solution.

citations.quote: Assume the Axiom of Choice, as used by the complete variational, Sobolev-extension and compact-spectral suppliers. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain. Define $H(\operatorname{curl})=\{u\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{curl}u\in L^2\}$ and $H(\operatorname{div})=\{u\in L^2:\operatorname{div}u\in L^2\}$ with their graph norms, and let $X$ be the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$; this is an explicit weak perfect-electric-conductor boundary class. Put $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline{V}^{\,L^2}$. Then the curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity tending to infinity whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and the zero eigenspace is finite dimensional and must be retained when the topology allows it. Each eigenfield $u_j\in V$ satisfies the full graph-class variational identity $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda_j\int_\Omega u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$. The eigen equation is $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ distributionally with the PEC trace, and for every explicitly chosen mathematical speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and every initial displacement $q_0\in V$ and velocity $q_1\in H$, the associated second-order wave has coefficients $a_j''+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_ja_j=0$ with those initial coefficients. Its displacement lies in $C(\mathbb R;V)$ and its velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$; finite modal sums converge respectively in $C(K;V)$ and $C(K;H)$ on every compact time interval $K$. The finite-dimensional $\lambda=0$ sector is retained with $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. This speed is a positive abstract mathematical parameter, not a physical constant or prerequisite. No identification with every maximal tangential-trace realisation, and no lossy, open or non-smooth-domain spectral claim, is made.
